calls.reason: Anthropic confirms retail token prices, while Cursor describes paid overages. Neither establishes actual subscriber costs or how often ordinary users generate losses.

The filing supports multibillion-dollar losses, but The Decoder's WSJ account identifies customers switching because of outages, including Retool. That undermines the central inference that continued enrollment means capacity problems do not affect growth.

Anthropic's October incident reports show service problems, and its June filing shows substantial cash. Neither establishes liquidity when the incidents occurred or a connection between degradation and cash pressure.

Goldman Sachs reports one company approaching inference spending of 10% of engineering headcount costs. It provides no operational results for that company, leaving the claimed absence of gains unresolved.
Bessemer reports positive gross margins across AI businesses, but does not isolate subscription economics. The packet lacks evidence showing how widely subscriptions operate below serving costs.
Anthropic links additional compute to higher usage limits, supporting a service benefit. Its announcement does not establish the resulting costs or whether added capacity also benefits growth.
